Rāmāyaṇa
epic poem, of the great Ṛṣi Vālmīki is well known to all Sanskrit scholars an. is a sacred book of the Hindus. Divided into seven Cantos or kāṇḍas viz. I. Bālakāṇḍa, II. Ayodhyākāṇḍa, III. Āraṇyakāṇḍa, IV. Kiṣkindhākāṇḍa, V. Sundarakāṇḍa, VI. Yuddhakāṇḍa an. VII. Uttarakāṇḍa. [Page001-b]
This epic has four variant Recensions viz. (I) Southern Recension (2) Gaudian or Bengali Recension (3) Western an. (4) North Western recension. According to Gaudian recension, the Bālakāṇḍa is called Ādikāṇḍa an. the Yuddhakāṇḍa is called Laṅkākānḍa. For more details of these recensions of the Rāmāyaṇa, see A Critical Inventory of Rāmāyaṇa Studies in the World. Vol. I. p.. xxiv to xxvii. ed. by K. Krishnamoorthy, Sahitya Acadami, New Delhi, 1991.
